notes: §1985:XVI.3.3.3 SRL2.1: a MERGE in an independent segment names an output procedure "Totally within non-independent segments, or" wholly within its own independent segment. Segmentation.RangeAllowed admits an all-fixed procedure from any segment and an independent one only when it is the MERGE's own (COBOL6877 otherwise), reached from SortBinder.BindMerge/CheckSegmentation at 85; the witness MERGE in 60 with OUTPUT 10 THRU 70 is refused. Probes at --std 85 (work-rd-11): s04 MERGE in 0 OUTPUT P-1 (60) THRU O-9 (70) refused COBOL6877 'segments 60, 70', s08 MERGE in 60 OUTPUT in 70 refused, s05 MERGE in 60 OUTPUT in 60 and s06 MERGE in 60 OUTPUT in fixed 49 accepted and ran with USING sequential files (DONE); MERGE has no INPUT PROCEDURE, so only its output procedure is checked (SortBinder.BindMerge); c edition arm: e01 (COBOL0902 at 2002+, --permissive does not ask the rule); a, d, f do not reach a procedure-placement rule.

next.reason: 1985: "Totally within non-independent segments, or"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the Segmentation module; no candidate addresses segments or program-flow restrictions". No 2023 clause holds the Segmentation feature, and no candidate mentions segments. The 2023 standard lacks non-independent segments, so this program-flow restriction is gone.
